role.altitude: The earth science teacher keeps writing the research case, leading the department, maintaining equipment and meeting students; rebuilding track records and budgets, compiling allocations and lists and keeping equipment spreadsheets shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping publication and asset records current
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose admin assembles from records already kept.

tasks.short: Read the call, develop the project with co-applicants, write the research case, update CV and publication list, write the data management plan and institutional sections, build the budget, correspond with co-applicants and the grants office, revise, fill the funder portal, check, sign off and submit grant proposals to procure external research funding.

steps.what: Teacher reads the funding call and rules
Teacher develops the project with co-applicants
Teacher writes the research case, aims and methods of grant proposals
Teacher updates the CV and publication list for the proposal
Teacher writes the data management plan and institutional sections
Teacher builds the budget in a spreadsheet from salary scales and rates
Teacher corresponds with co-applicants and the grants office
Teacher revises the proposal after comments
Teacher fills the funder portal forms
Teacher checks the final proposal in the portal: the research case, budget and attachments match the call and what co-applicants agreed, and obtains institutional sign-off
Teacher submits the approved proposal to the funder

approvals.approved_version: The proposal, budget and portal entries exactly as checked and signed off in s10, submitted once to the funder named in the call; any change needs a new check and sign-off.

tasks.design: The CV and publication list are generated from the publication database and CV record, and the teacher checks them. Data management and institutional sections start from the institution's template library. A budget template holds current salary scales and rates. The funder account prefills applicant details in the portal. The research case, co-applicant work, revision, sign-off and submission stay with the teacher, and no proposal text goes to tools that breach confidentiality.
tasks.previous_blocker: Track record, boilerplate and rates were rebuilt for each proposal.
tasks.enabler_now: Publication databases, template libraries and budget templates.
tasks.still_hard: Consortium proposals with many partners' rates.
tasks.human_edge: Framing a question reviewers will want answered.
tasks.altitude: Less boilerplate; the research case stays.

evidence.claim: A national research funder bars generative AI for its referees and hidden prompts in applications; uploading a proposal breaches confidentiality.
Grant proposals suit a generator from publications and templates; the teacher signs.

assumptions: Boundary: writing grant proposals; conducting research (task 5845) is a sibling task.
The means prior puts 59% on documents and 15% on screens; the steps show about 68% on documents and 9% on screens, because the research case and its revision take most of the time.

s4 keeps 30 for checking the generated CV and list; s5 keeps 70 because templates give the standard parts and the plan is still written for this project; s6 keeps 60 because rates no longer need looking up but planning staff months and costs stays; s9 keeps 80 because most portal fields still need the proposal's own text.
research_questions: Do proposals go to the grants office earlier?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the publication record current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the template library lacks this funder's formats and the budget template lags behind new rates, so s5 keeps 90 and s6 keeps 80 (7.5); high: templates current as assumed (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Chair department meetings, meet staff one to one, meet faculty management, read policies and requests, write plans and memos, build the teaching allocation, approve leave and expenses, compile annual report figures, check budget reports and answer mail to perform administrative duties such as serving as department head.

steps.what: Teacher chairs department meetings as department head
Teacher meets staff one to one about workload and development
Teacher meets faculty management
Teacher reads policies, reports and requests
Teacher writes department plans, memos and replies to the faculty
Teacher builds the teaching allocation in a spreadsheet from course lists and contract hours
Teacher approves leave, travel and expense requests
Teacher compiles annual report figures from several systems
Teacher checks department budget reports
Teacher answers staff and faculty mail

tasks.design: An allocation tool reads courses from the catalogue and hours from contracts and shows totals per person, and the head decides who teaches what, instead of building the spreadsheet. A department dashboard gives the annual report figures. Meetings, reading, writing, approvals, budget checks and mail stay with the head.
tasks.previous_blocker: Allocations and report figures were compiled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Allocation tools on catalogue and contract data, and department dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing workloads fairly when staff are on leave.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a department together through budget cuts.

evidence.claim: Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent.
Reports are generated from source systems instead of rekeying into Excel.

assumptions: Boundary: department head duties; serving on committees (task 5863) is a sibling task.
The allocation tool uses only contract hours and courses, not performance or traits; the works council consents.
The means prior puts 5% on spreadsheets; the steps show 10%, for the allocation and budget checks.
s6 keeps half for the decisions; s8 keeps 40.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the dashboard does not hold the annual report figures, so s8 stays 100 (3.5); high: dashboard and allocation tool as assumed (7.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Specify requirements, request and compare quotes, write purchase justifications, enter purchase requests, receive and install equipment, maintain and calibrate it, book service visits, keep the inventory and service dates and file manuals and certificates to purchase and maintain equipment to support research projects.

steps.what: Teacher specifies equipment requirements with colleagues and vendors
Teacher requests quotes by mail
Teacher compares quotes
Teacher writes the purchase justification
Teacher enters purchase requests in the procurement system
Teacher checks the final purchase request: equipment, specification, supplier and price match the chosen quote and the justification
Teacher submits the checked purchase request in the procurement system
Teacher receives and installs equipment
Teacher maintains, calibrates and repairs research equipment
Teacher writes the service visit request to the vendor
Teacher checks the final service request: instrument, fault or due calibration, dates and vendor are right
Teacher sends the checked service request to the vendor
Teacher keeps the equipment inventory and service dates in a spreadsheet
Teacher files manuals, calibration certificates and service reports

tasks.design: Equipment bought through the procurement system is added to an asset register with service and calibration dates and reminders, with manuals and certificates attached, instead of a separate spreadsheet and folders. Requirements, quotes, the justification, the request, installation, maintenance and service bookings stay with the teacher, who checks each request and booking before it goes out.

approvals.approved_version: The purchase request with equipment, specification, supplier and price exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, submitted once to purchasing in the procurement system; any change needs a new check.
The service visit request with instrument, work needed and dates exactly as checked by the teacher in s8a, sent once by mail to the named vendor; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment data were kept in a separate list and folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Asset registers linked to procurement with reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Old equipment with no purchase record.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which instrument will survive field conditions.
tasks.altitude: Less list keeping; equipment care stays.

reach.learn: Whether calibration is up to date.

evidence.claim: Excel lists and folders move into records apps with notifications.

assumptions: Boundary: purchasing and maintaining research equipment; selecting textbooks and course equipment (task 5862) is a sibling task.

s9 keeps 30 for equipment bought before the register; s10 keeps half for attaching each file. Entering, checking and submitting requests and writing, checking and sending service bookings keep their full time.
The means prior puts 10% on screens; the steps show 6%, because entering the request is the only screen work and maintenance dominates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much older equipment stays outside the register, so s9 keeps 60 and s10 keeps 80 (3.4); high: most equipment in the register as assumed (6.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare open day materials, present at open days and fairs, talk with prospective students, answer their mail, review applications and interview applicants, compile applicant lists, check registration status, mail placement partners, write, check and send placement agreements to participate in student recruitment, registration and placement.

steps.what: Teacher prepares open day materials
Teacher presents at open days and fairs to recruit students
Teacher talks with prospective students and parents
Teacher answers prospective students' mail: writing each reply today, editing a draft that cites the programme's approved pages after the change

loop.input: The question and the programme's approved pages.
loop.output: A draft reply citing the page it uses.
loop.check: The teacher checks that each draft answers the question asked and that the cited page says what the reply claims, and edits every reply; questions the pages do not cover are answered by hand.
loop.stop: Questions about an individual application go to the teacher unanswered.
loop.why_not_simpler: Students ask in their own words.

steps.what: Teacher checks the final reply: it answers the question, and dates, rules and links are right for this programme
Teacher sends the checked reply to the prospective student
Teacher compiles applicant lists from the admissions system into spreadsheets
Teacher reviews applications
Teacher interviews applicants
Teacher checks registration status of admitted students one by one
Teacher mails placement partners
Teacher writes placement agreements
Teacher checks the final placement agreements: student, partner, dates, tasks and supervision match what was arranged
Teacher sends the approved agreements to placement partners

approvals.approved_version: Each placement agreement exactly as checked by the teacher in s11, sent once to the named partner; any change needs a new check.
Each reply exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the prospective student who asked; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Replies to prospective students start from drafts citing the programme's approved pages, and the teacher edits each, checks it against the question and sends it once. The admissions system's views replace the applicant spreadsheet and show registration status as a list. Placement agreements fill student and partner details from the records. Presenting, conversations, reviewing applications, interviews, partner mail, checking and sending stay with the teacher. No model assesses applicants.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lists were compiled by hand and agreements typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Draft replies from approved pages, admissions system views and agreement templates.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a student who will thrive despite weak grades.
tasks.altitude: Less list keeping; recruitment stays personal.

evidence.claim: Admission is a high-risk education use, so no model assesses applicants.

assumptions: Boundary: recruitment, registration and placement; advising students on curricula and careers (task 5858) is a sibling task.
The means prior puts 14% on mail; the steps show about 19%, because prospective-student and partner mail are frequent.

s4 is priced at 70 because every draft is read and edited; checking and sending each reply keep their full time; s5 keeps 30; s8 keeps half; s10 keeps half for the tasks and supervision written per placement.
research_questions: Do prospective students get answers sooner?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most questions fall outside the approved pages, so s4 keeps 90 (10.9); high: drafts usable for most mail as assumed (12.9).
